content_sections.heading: Karnataka High Court Civil Judge Eligibility Criteria 2026
content_sections.text: The Karnataka Civil Judge Recruitment 2026 eligibility criteria are governed by the Karnataka Judicial Service (Recruitment) Rules, 2004, and subsequent amendments. Candidates must possess the prescribed Law Degree, required professional experience and satisfy the applicable age and service conditions. Applicants must possess a Degree in Law (LLB) granted by a university established by law in India. In addition, the supplementary notification requires qualifying legal practice or Government legal service experience. Candidates must fulfil the prescribed Law Degree and professional experience requirements. Merely possessing an LLB degree without the required qualifying experience does not establish eligibility. The minimum age for Karnataka Civil Judge Recruitment 2026 is 18 years. The supplementary notification specifies category-wise upper age limits along with an additional one-time relaxation of five years provided under Government Order No. DPAR 262 SeNeNi 2025 dated 29 January 2026. Important: The additional five-year relaxation is a one-time measure applicable to all categories under the cited Government Order. The notification also provides an additional three-year upper age relaxation for eligible Ex-Servicemen.

content_sections.heading: Karnataka Civil Judge Training and Appointment 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates selected for Karnataka Civil Judge Recruitment 2026 will initially be appointed as Trainee Judicial Officers. They must undergo one year of intensive training at the Karnataka Judicial Academy, followed by one year of structured Law Clerkship. The Recruitment Authority will evaluate the candidate's performance and suitability before recommending appointment as Civil Judge. Candidates whose performance is found unsatisfactory may be rejected. During training and clerkship, Trainee Judicial Officers do not have an automatic right to appointment as Civil Judges. Selected candidates must also pass the Kannada Language Examination conducted by the Karnataka Public Service Commission under the applicable Karnataka Civil Services rules.

content_sections.heading: Karnataka High Court Civil Judge Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: The Karnataka High Court Civil Judge Selection Process 2026 consists of three main competitive examination stages: Preliminary Examination, Main Written Examination and Viva-voce. Candidates must also undergo a Computer Test. The final selection is subject to the minimum qualifying marks, merit, verification and applicable judicial service recruitment rules. The Preliminary Examination will consist of objective-type questions carrying 100 marks. It tests candidates' knowledge of Civil Law, Criminal Law, the Constitution and General Knowledge, including reasoning and mental ability. Candidates shortlisted from the Preliminary Examination will appear for the Main Written Examination, which consists of four papers carrying 100 marks each. The papers cover translation, legal knowledge, civil judgment writing and criminal judgment writing. Candidates qualifying in the Main Written Examination will be called for Viva-voce carrying 100 marks. The interview will assess general knowledge, understanding of legal principles and suitability for appointment as a Civil Judge. A separate Computer Test carrying 25 marks will assess candidates' computer knowledge and suitability. Marks obtained in the Computer Test will not be added to the total marks secured in the Main Written Examination and Viva-voce. Shortlisted candidates must produce the prescribed original certificates and supporting documents for verification. Final selection will be based on the applicable examination results, qualifying standards, eligibility verification and recruitment rules.

content_sections.heading: Karnataka Civil Judge Preliminary Exam Pattern 2026
content_sections.text: The Karnataka Civil Judge Preliminary Examination 2026 consists of an objective-type question paper carrying 100 marks. The syllabus is divided into Part A, Part B and Part C, covering Civil Law, Criminal Law and General Knowledge. Question Type: Objective. Maximum Marks: 100. Minimum Qualifying Marks: 50 for SC, ST and PwBD candidates; 60 for other candidates. The notification does not specify a separate number of questions or marks for each of the three syllabus parts in the preliminary examination.

content_sections.heading: Karnataka Civil Judge Minimum Qualifying Marks 2026
content_sections.text: The Karnataka High Court has prescribed separate minimum qualifying marks for the Preliminary Examination, each paper of the Main Written Examination and Viva-voce. Candidates must meet the applicable qualifying standards to proceed to the next stage. For consideration under the General category, SC, ST and PwBD candidates must meet the General-category qualifying standards of 60 marks in the Preliminary Examination, 50 marks in each Main Written Examination paper and 25 marks in Viva-voce. The notification provides for calling, as far as practicable, candidates up to ten times the number of category-wise vacancies for the Main Written Examination and up to three times the vacancies for Viva-voce, subject to eligibility and merit.

faq.answer: The Preliminary Examination is an objective-type test carrying 100 marks, covering Civil Law, Criminal Law, the Constitution, General Knowledge, reasoning and mental ability.
